Messages.Author: TigersClaw
Messages.Body:
What happens in a four player game if, #4 call a domain challege and it
passes and player #2 and #3 are ousted at the same time? How are blood
(6) and victory points done.? Done player #1 who remain get 12 pool and
2 points? Also #4 remain in game.
Numbering used to represent table positions?

Larry

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
In article <342C88...@iquest.net>, lpic...@iquest.net wrote:
>
> What happens in a four player game if, #4 call a domain challege and it
> passes and player #2 and #3 are ousted at the same time? How are blood
> (6) and victory points done.? Done player #1 who remain get 12 pool and
> 2 points? Also #4 remain in game.

VtES rules, section 10: If a predator is ousted the same turn her prey
is ousted, the predator gets the victory point, but does not get six
blood points.

#2 gets a VP (since #3 is ousted).
#1 gets a VP (since #3 is ousted).
#1 gets 6 pool (since #1 is still in the game).

> Numbering used to represent table positions?

Yes. :-)

Messages.Author: Dave Green
Messages.Body:
TigersClaw <lpic...@iquest.net> wrote:
: What happens in a four player game if, #4 call a domain challege and it
: passes and player #2 and #3 are ousted at the same time? How are blood
: (6) and victory points done.? Done player #1 who remain get 12 pool and
: 2 points? Also #4 remain in game.

: Numbering used to represent table positions?

: Larry

Player #1 would get one victory point and 6 pool for having his
prey (#2) ousted. #2 would get 1 victory point for having his
prey (#3) ousted, but is no longer around to recieve the 6
pool, and is still ousted himself. #3 is just ousted,
recieving nothing, and #4 remains and gains nothing for his
efforts except a smaller field of play.

-Dave Green
advocate of common sense and a return to innocence for Jyhad
